earlier_scan.source_named: Extinct ancient Near Eastern language attested only in names; Glottolog lists only areal overviews (Goldammer 2011; Kausen 2013); no phonological description exists

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Gutian language' (accessed 2026-09-17), citing Hallo, Jacobsen 1939, Henning 1978, Michalowski 2017.
sources.note: States no linguistic features are known beyond Jacobsen's suggested -(e)sh ending; corpus = king-list names, Sag B school list mention, Adab interpreter tablet.

sources.citation: Streck, Michael P. 2024. »Seine Sprache war fremd, niemand verstand seine Rede.« Indirekte Sprachzeugnisse im Alten Orient. Sitzungsberichte der Sächsischen Akademie der Wissenschaften zu Leipzig, Philologisch-historische Klasse, Band 143, Heft 5. Stuttgart: S. Hirzel (in Kommission). 31 pp. ISBN 978-3-7776-3544-6 (print), 978-3-7776-3548-4 (e-book); open access.
sources.note: Nothing. The essay (Akademie Sitzungsbericht on indirect language attestations in the Ancient Near East) mentions Gutian only as a language listed in a Late Babylonian text on the languages of the world (p. 15) and as a language for which interpreters are attested in Ur III administrative texts (p. 17, ch. 4 A); it states explicitly that Gutian was never written and is barely known. No phonological or prosodic content anywhere in the 31 pages (a full-text search for stress/accent Akzent/Betonung/Ton/Silbe: no hits).

sources.citation: Алимирзоев, А. Н. [Alimirzoev, A. N.] 2019. Из политической истории кутиев [From the political history of the Gutians]. Вестник Дагестанского государственного университета. Серия 2: Гуманитарные науки 34(1). Махачкала.
sources.note: No phonology. Calls Gutian 'бесписьменный кутийский язык' (unwritten), reports that some scholars took it for a proto-Northeast-Caucasian language (citing instability of initial k- in that group for Guti ~ uti), and offers etymologies of name elements (iar- ~ Urartian iarani 'temple', Gutian harambi ~ Hurrian erembi 'juniper', tali 'tree'). Zero occurrences of ударение/фонетика/тон.
sources.venue: Вестник Дагестанского государственного университета. Серия 2: Гуманитарные науки

sources.citation: Алимирзоев, А. Н. 2018. Кто был третьим правителем Кутиума [Who was the third ruler of Gutium]. Проблемы истории, филологии, культуры 4(62): 42-48. DOI 10.18503/1992-0431-2018-4-62-42-48.
sources.note: No phonology content: cuneiform sign-reading argument about the third king's name (logogram + phonetic complement vs syllabic reading ia-ku-la-ab = Yakulaba); bibliography points to Balkan 1992 [=1990] Erdem and Дьяконов 1956 История Мидии.

sources.citation: Гамкрелидзе, Т. В. & Иванов, Вяч. Вс. 2013. Индоевропейская прародина и расселение индоевропейцев: полвека исследований и обсуждений [Indo-European homeland and migrations: half a century of studies and discussions]. Вопросы языкового родства / Journal of Language Relationship 9: 109-136. DOI 10.31826/jlr-2013-090111.
sources.note: Nothing about Gutian stress, accent or tone. The only 'ударение/акцентуация' in the article (p. 113 fn.) concerns loss of -r in Hittite verb forms. On Gutian it says Henning proposed that the ancestors of the Tocharians formed the ruling dynasty of the Gutians, that the authors developed this from the ethnonyms Guti/Tukri ~ Kuchean/Tocharian, and that 'some possible etymologies of the names of Gutian kings' support it (referring to VDI 1989 and Gamkrelidze & Ivanov 2006); no forms are analysed here.
sources.venue: Вопросы языкового родства / Journal of Language Relationship

sources.citation: Kausen, Ernst. 2001. Altorientalische Restsprachen: Übersicht über die Sprachen des Alten Orients; Hattisch, Kassitisch, Gutäisch und Lulubäisch. Web manuscript (Word document, '© 2001'), Fachhochschule Gießen-Friedberg / THM homepage of Prof. Ernst Kausen. 7,200 characters. [Precursor of the section 'Gutäisch-Lulubäisch' in Kausen 2013, Die Sprachfamilien der Welt I (Buske), which round 1 listed as print-only.]
sources.note: Nothing on phonology at all. The whole Gutian section is historical and ends: 'Gutäisch-lulubäische Sprachreste sind nur als Personennamen und verstreut in lexikalischen Listen erhalten.' The introduction says 'Der Überlieferungszustand dieser Sprachen - Hattisch, Kassitisch, Gutäisch und Lulubäisch - ist allerdings sehr schlecht, en[t]sprechend kurz sind die Darstellungen' and 'Ob das fast unbekannte Lulubäische mit dem Gutäischen wirklich.. genetisch verwandt ist, lässt sich bei der Dürftig[k]eit des vorliegenden Materials kaum abschließend klären.' Term count Akzent/Betonung/Ton/Silbe/Laut…
sources.venue: Web manuscript (Word document, '© 2001'), Fachhochschule Gießen-Friedberg / THM homepage of Prof

sources.citation: Balkan, Kemal. 1990. Relations Between the Language of the Gutians and Old Turkish. Erdem (Atatürk Kültür Merkezi Dergisi) 6(16): 65-126. Ankara. [Turkish version: 'Eski Önasya'da Kut (veya Gut) Halkının Dili ile Eski Türkçe Arasındaki Benzerlik', same issue pp. 1-64,https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/692701]
sources.note: No mention of stress, accent, tone, pitch or syllable structure anywhere in 62 pp. (extracted text full text searched and the sound passages read). Content: reprint of Landsberger 1937 (German), then p.82: 'In the present study I have collected the following subjects concerning the Gutian language: word roots, word structures, personal names, treasury of the Gutian words and some sounds peculiar to the Gu[t]ian language'; commentary on each king name (pp. 90-101) with segmental remarks only (variant spellings Sarlag/Assarlag/Iarlagab taken to render an initial sound hard to write in cuneiform…

sources.citation: Дьяконов, И. М. & Старостин, С. А. Хуррито-урартские и восточнокавказские языки [Russian version of Diakonoff & Starostin 1986, Hurro-Urartian as an Eastern Caucasian Language]. In: Старостин, С. А. 2007. Труды по языкознанию. Москва: Языки славянских культур, pp. 359ff; Gutian paragraph on p. 362 with fn. 10.
sources.note: One paragraph: Gutian was 'probably another ancient language of the East Caucasian family'; 'from it practically only a few dozen proper names are known'; some Sumerian loanwords of non-Hurrian EC origin might be Gutian; 'it may have been close to Lezgian' (Udi < *Quti- suggestion). No phonology of Gutian itself; the phonological table that follows is Proto-East-Caucasian, not Gutian.

sources.citation: Hallo, William W. 1971. Gutium (Qutium). Reallexikon der Assyriologie und Vorderasiatischen Archäologie 3: 708-720. Berlin: de Gruyter. (BAdW open page scan)
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 11 'Gutian linguistic remains' (p. 719): 'The available Gutian personal names do not suffice for even a tentative restoration of a Gutian language'; corpus = ruler names, two plant-name glosses (hara[mbi], elinu) in synonym lists, one deity name Abublab; Babylonians called the language 'confused'; a Gutian dragoman attested in Sargonic times.
sources.venue: Reallexikon der Assyriologie und Vorderasiatischen Archäologie

sources.citation: Jacobsen, Thorkild. 1939. The Sumerian King List. Assyriological Studies 11. Chicago: Oriental Institute of the University of Chicago.
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Only linguistic remarks on Gutian: p. 119 n. 301 argues for 'a nasalized g in Gutian' from variant spellings ia-ar-la-gab / ia-ar-la-an-gab; p. 207 (with n. 40) 'Elulumesh.. Akkadian Elulum slightly Gutianized by the Gutian case(?) ending -esh'. Gutian dynasty name list pp. 116-121.

sources.citation: Speiser, Ephraim A. 1930. Mesopotamian Origins: The Basic Population of the Near East. Philadelphia: University of Pennsylvania Press; London: Humphrey Milford, Oxford University Press. xiii+198 pp. (Chapter IV 'The Lullu and the Guti', pp. 88-119: 'Gutian personal names.. Phonetic peculiarities.. Alleged relationship of Gutians and Indo-Europeans').
sources.note: The only linguistic analysis is segmental/morphological: recurring name-final elements (-b 'with an overhanging vowel', -sh 'probably only a simple s-sound', -n, -ak, -am), the formative -laga-, and one 'phonetic peculiarity', an initial tl-like sound inferred from Ja-/Ta- spelling variants (Lagalaga/Tagalaga), shared with Elamite and Lullubian; concludes 'the linguistic position of the Gutians is distinctly within the larger Zagros group'. No word on accent, stress or tone anywhere in the chapter (full-text search: 'accent' occurs once, about an Elamite vowel in a-wa-a-ak; 'stress'/'tone' on…
Areal/historical overview with bibliography; blocked by an automated-access block by automated download. Would not add a stress statement.

sources.citation: Michalowski, Piotr. 2017. Ancient Near Eastern and European isolates. In Lyle Campbell (ed.), Language Isolates, 19-58. London: Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent specialist survey of Gutian as a linguistic entity; would confirm (second-hand) that nothing beyond onomastics is recoverable. Cannot contain a stress rule.
